key_insight: Injecting logical-level noise lets large IQP quantum circuit Born machines be broken into smaller clusters that can be sampled on qubit-limited hardware while preserving key correlations better than a classical marginal-matching baseline.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical deployment strategy for running trained quantum generative models on today’s smaller quantum processors without retraining the model architecture.
method: Train large IQP-QCBMs classically even when the circuit exceeds hardware qubit count.
Inject noise at the logical level to probabilistically decompose the circuit into smaller sampleable clusters.
Use lightweight resampling of known noisy qubits to mitigate error during hardware execution.
evidence_signal: Simulations on shallow IQP QCBMs and IBM Heron experiments deploying a 316-qubit IQP circuit onto 156-qubit hardware showed improved similarity to the target distribution after mitigation.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate noise modeling and mitigation, so performance may vary when hardware noise differs from the assumed logical-level decomposition.
paper_title: Deployment of Large IQP Circuit Born Machines on Qubit-Limited Hardware Using Noise Injection
